name: Daylight
summary: A tablet with a paper-like display for reading, writing and using apps.
audience: Readers and people who want a calmer place to write or take notes.
technology: A reflective display designed for fluid interaction and use in sunlight.
why: It asks how the physical qualities of a screen can change the feeling of using a computer. A useful reference for Commonwealth's paper-inspired interface.
freshness: New to Commonwealth, not a newly launched product. The maker's page includes reactions dated May 2024.
caveat: Product features are described by the manufacturer; health and attention benefits are not independently established here.

sources.title: Daylight — product and company
sources.evidence: Describes a paper-like display, reading, writing, app support and sunlight use.

name: Looking Glass Go
summary: A portable display for viewing 3D memories and creative work without a headset.
audience: People displaying personal images and creators experimenting with spatial imagery.
technology: Light-field display technology presents multiple perspectives so digital images can appear to have depth.
why: It gives a digital memory a physical place in a room. It could inspire us to think about how saved ideas are displayed and revisited.
freshness: New to Commonwealth; this run did not verify a launch date.
caveat: Go is distinct from the company's newer large-format displays. The maker says Go has no included battery; portable does not mean cordless.

sources.title: Looking Glass — Go and light-field displays
sources.evidence: Describes Go, headset-free viewing and light-field perspectives; its FAQ says a battery is not included.

name: Playdate
summary: A pocket game console with a hand crank that controls actions in some games.
audience: Players and independent developers interested in unusual, small-scale games.
technology: Digital games respond to an analog crank alongside conventional buttons.
why: A simple physical gesture becomes a creative constraint. It is a strong reference for making Commonwealth's tear-off interaction feel purposeful.
freshness: An established reference newly added to our research queue, not presented as a recent startup.
caveat: The crank is a controller, not a charger, and not every game uses it. This is the first pipeline calibration batch, not a roundup of new launches.

sources.title: Playdate — system and crank
sources.evidence: Describes the crank as an analog controller and credits Teenage Engineering for the hardware design collaboration.
